scope.current_boundary: Teach the physical concept of work as mechanical energy transfer, the formal definition of work done as force multiplied by displacement in the direction of the force, the resolved force formula W = Fs cos theta, positive, negative, and zero work conditions, work done as the area under a force-displacement graph, work done by expanding gas at constant pressure W = p Delta V, and the foundational role of work in the principle of conservation of energy. Do not pre-teach quantitative efficiency formulas, power calculations (P = W/t, P = Fv), or gravitational and kinetic energy formulas (Delta E_P = mg Delta h, E_K = 1/2 m v^2).
prior_scope_summaries_consulted: Assumes mastery of vector resolution and trigonometry from Topic 1, linear kinematics and displacement from Topic 2, Newton's laws of motion and resultant forces from Topic 3, and pressure definition p = F / A from Topic 4.

immediate_previous.boundary: No prior lesson in Topic 5; this is the introductory lesson of Topic 5 (Work, energy and power).
can_assume: Newton's laws of motion and equilibrium
hydrostatic pressure definition p = F / A

immediate_next.boundary: Conservation of energy, energy dissipation into thermal stores, and quantitative efficiency problems.
must_not_preteach: quantitative efficiency formula useful output / total input * 100%
power as work done per unit time
